incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: INC-2026 - canary-service-high-5xx in us-east-1. Trigger: canary failure rate > 3% over 2m. Link: <https://pagerduty.example/INC-2026>
pagerduty: PagerDuty: notification sent to schedule 'sre-oncall'. Autopage: primary not responding within 30s.
Eve: I got the page, jumping on this now. What signal exactly?
incident-bot: Detected elevated 5xx rate (502/504) for route /v1/generate on model-serving-canary-2026. Canary instances returning 502s at ~6% of requests, baseline 0.2%.
Bob: Looking at logs in us-east-1 canary nodes. Seeing fast failures with stack trace referencing attention-kernel. Pasting tail of errors:
```
2026-03-14T21:12:05Z ERROR worker-3 model: inference failed: cuda runtime error: out of memory
  at runtime/kernel.cu:432
```
Alice: Hmm we just rolled canary bundle 2026.03.14-r1 10m ago. The release had a new attention kernel patch and a different quant profile. Could be regression.
Carla: Support has two customers reporting increased 502 errors in EU/US. Impact: degraded interactive features, ~5% of sessions affected, no data loss reported.
Dan: We need a clear customer-facing statement. For now we should say we are investigating and may rollback canary if needed.
Eve: First mitigation: isolate canary from traffic. I am switching the routing policy to send 0% to model-serving-canary via rollout API now.
Eve: `curl -X POST https://console.redwood/rollouts/canary/adjust -d '{"weight":0}'` -> 200 OK
incident-bot: Canary weight updated to 0%. Traffic will drain in ~30s.
Bob: Confirmed 5xx rate dropped on prod routes after removing canary. Canary pods still showing OOMs in logs.
Alice: Starting a rollback of the canary image to previous stable tag `2026.03.07-stable`. Running `kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-serving-canary --to-revision=3`.
Frank: I'll open a quick incident bridge and start a short postmortem doc. Bridge: <https://meet.example/bridge/INC-2026>
Carla: Notifying affected customers with interim message: "We've detected elevated errors impacting a small subset of requests. We've removed the canary from rotation and are investigating. We'll update in 30 minutes."
Eve: Initiated `kubectl rollout undo` -> rollout started. Monitoring memory and 5xx.
Bob: After rollback start, canary pod restarts show kernel backtrace gone. 5xx rate for canary dropped from 6% -> 0.3% over 2m.
Dan: Good. Can we confirm no regression in latency or other metrics after rollback? Alice?
Alice: Quick smoke checks look ok. CPU spiked briefly while pods restarted but latencies returned to baseline within 2m. Adding an artifact note: regression introduced by attention-kernel v1.12 with different scratch-buffer sizing.
Eve: I'm going to mark the page acknowledged in PD and close the active incident. PD: `ack INC-2026` -> acknowledged by Eve.
pagerduty: INC-2026 acknowledged by Eve.
Frank: Notes for follow-up: (1) block the problematic kernel until we have proper OOM checks; (2) add load-safety gate to canary so OOMs don't reach PD thresholds; (3) schedule root-cause triage with eng-runtime and research tomorrow.
Carla: Support will follow up with customers using template and offer compensation where needed. Tracking ticket #SUP-889.
Bob: Will capture heap/dump from the canary pods and attach to the postmortem doc.
Alice: I'll revert the quant profile change on staging and run stress tests. Tentative fix: adjust scratch buffer allocation and guardrail on batch-size.
Eve: Handoff: I'm ending my shift in 3h. Leaving monitoring alerts for follow-up to Bob (next oncall). I'll DM Bob the checklist.
Bob: Copy that — I'll take secondary on this. If anything spikes, page me on PD.
Frank: Postmortem doc started: <https://docs.redwood/incs/INC-2026>. I'll tag owners and set P1 -> P2 for follow-up tasks.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026 status -> Resolved. Root cause: regression in attention kernel causing OOMs on new canary bundle; mitigation: removed canary, rolled back to stable, customers see restored service.
Eve: Closing thread. Great cross-team execution. :thumbsup:
summary: Canary deployment caused OOMs -> PagerDuty page -> canary removed & rolled back -> service restored; follow-ups assigned
